issue.title: Enable serial and TCP connections for backend
issue.body:
The backend currently only supports UDP and the port is hardcoded for the backend_bin.

We should use `add_any_connection`, so that we can pass any connection URI.

comments.body:
Hello,

I was wondering today about the same issue on larger scale (Not exactly for Serial), Maybe we can improve the parser, to accept string and numbers instead of a connection URI.
For instance defining the connection type, UDP, TCP, or Serial and the ip address and the port number differently. This is easier for the user to specify some numbers instead of the entire URI. The less we type, the less error user can have
What do you think?
@shrit: Would you have examples illustrating what you mean (instead of the connection URI)?
We already support shortening where applicable, e.g. `udp://` will use the default port on localhost.

well, actually after creating an instance of 
DronecodeSDK dc_;
we call the function 
dc_.add_any_connection(string);
the string variable contain the entire URI. For example, in the example of documentation we have:
udp://:14540
in the case twe are on udp on localhost  with the port 14540.

A rare use case, If we need to control several vehicles, several instance of controller should be created and we need to specify for each on the port and the connection type.
For this reason, I thought of simplifying even more for the users, like a user could type -P 14540 14550 14560, that is going to take a vector of port number for a set of vehicles.

I would argue that's too rare of a use case. I would then just have the cli be a list, e.g.: `foo udp://:14540 udp://:14541` and then loop through it.

And note that you can have several vehicles connecting on the same UDP port at the same time, so you don't need a port per vehicle.

issue.title: Arming not working HITL in Python example

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
It seems like we can't arm (or we can't arm immediately) in HITL simulation due to the error `COMMAND_DENIED_LANDED_STATE_UNKNOWN`.

The question is if it's a timing issue or if our request to send `EXTENDED_SYS_STATE` at 1 Hz fails or is not supported.

FYI @JonasVautherin 

This works with C++ but seems to fail with this Python example:
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import asyncio

from dronecode_sdk import connect as dronecode_sdk_connect
from dronecode_sdk import start_mavlink

start_mavlink()
drone = dronecode_sdk_connect(host="127.0.0.1")


async def run():
    print("-- Arming")
    await drone.action.arm()
    print("-- Taking off")
    await drone.action.takeoff()
    await asyncio.sleep(5)
    print("-- Landing")
    await drone.action.land()

loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
loop.run_until_complete(run())

```
